1486,2020-03-26 18:00:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1487,2020-03-26 18:10:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1488,2020-03-26 18:20:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1489,2020-03-26 18:30:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1490,2020-03-26 18:40:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1491,2020-03-26 18:50:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1492,2020-03-26 19:00:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1493,2020-03-26 19:10:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1494,2020-03-26 19:20:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1495,2020-03-26 19:30:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1496,2020-03-26 19:40:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1497,2020-03-26 19:50:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1498,2020-03-26 20:00:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1499,2020-03-26 20:10:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
1500,2020-03-26 20:20:00,-22.5,-4.5,-25.5
"""
temp_data_raw = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv_data))
high_alarm = -15
low_alarm = -25
temp_data_raw = temp_data_raw.rename(columns={'Time':'date_time',
		'Celsius(°C)':'celsius',
		'High Alarm':'high_alarm',
		'Low Alarm':'low_alarm',
		'Serial Number':'serial_number'}
		)
temp_data_raw['date_time'] = pd.to_datetime(temp_data_raw['date_time'])
temp_data_raw = temp_data_raw.sort_values('date_time')
#Find spikes and add 'status' column, which will be used to filter spike max (if too_high) or min (if too_low) temperature:
temp_data_raw.loc[temp_data_raw['celsius'] > high_alarm, 'status'] = 'too_high'
temp_data_raw.loc[temp_data_raw['celsius'] < low_alarm, 'status'] = 'too_low'
#add cumulative spike id to be able to number spikes:
temp_data_raw['cumulat_spike_id'] = (temp_data_raw['status'] != temp_data_raw['status'].shift()).cumsum()

temp_data_raw['reading_gap_mins'] = temp_data_raw.groupby('cumulat_spike_id')['date_time'].diff().dt.total_seconds() / 60

temp_data = temp_data_raw[temp_data_raw['status'].isin(['too_high', 'too_low'])][['cumulat_spike_id','date_time','celsius','status']]

temp_data['last_spike_of_day'] = (
    (temp_data['date_time'].dt.date != temp_data['date_time'].dt.date.shift(-1))
)


temp_data['24hr_window_start'] = pd.to_datetime(np.where(
    temp_data['last_spike_of_day'],
    (temp_data['date_time'] - pd.Timedelta(hours=24)).dt.floor('s'),
    pd.NaT
))


df_last_spike_of_day = temp_data[temp_data['last_spike_of_day']==True][['date_time','last_spike_of_day','24hr_window_start']]

def spike_duration_in_window(row, temp_data):
    mask = (
        (temp_data['date_time'] >= row['24hr_window_start']) &
        (temp_data['date_time'] <= row['date_time']) &
        (temp_data['status'].isin(['too_high', 'too_low']))
    )
    
    filtered = temp_data.loc[mask].copy() 
    if filtered.empty:
        return 0
    
    return filtered['reading_gap_mins'].sum()

df_last_spike_of_day['spike_duration_24hr_mins'] = df_last_spike_of_day.apply(
    spike_duration_in_window, axis=1, temp_data=temp_data_raw
)

#obtain grouped temp data for each spike found:
temp_data_grouped = temp_data_raw[temp_data_raw['status'].isin(['too_high', 'too_low'])].groupby('cumulat_spike_id').agg(
    spike_status=('status','first'),
    spike_max_temp=('celsius', 'max'),
    spike_min_temp=('celsius', 'min'),
    spike_max_temp_id = ('celsius','idxmax'),
    spike_min_temp_id = ('celsius', 'idxmin'),
    spike_start_time=('date_time', 'min'),
    spike_end_time=('date_time', 'max')
)
#find spike duration in minutes:
temp_data_grouped['spike_duration_mins'] = ((temp_data_grouped['spike_end_time'] - temp_data_grouped['spike_start_time']).dt.total_seconds() / 60).astype(int)

#initiate id column for extreme temperature at which spike was observed:
temp_data_grouped['extreme_idx'] = temp_data_grouped['spike_max_temp_id'] #randomly set to spike_max_temp_id
temp_data_grouped.loc[temp_data_grouped['spike_status'] == 'too_low', 'extreme_idx'] = temp_data_grouped['spike_min_temp_id'] #re-write extreme id column values for when spike status is 'too_low'

#retrieve extreme spike temperature and date/time stamp using extreme id:
temp_data_grouped['extreme_temp'] = temp_data.loc[temp_data_grouped['extreme_idx'], 'celsius'].values
temp_data_grouped['extreme_date_time'] = temp_data.loc[temp_data_grouped['extreme_idx'], 'date_time'].values

#add spike id (consecutive number starting at 1) to be used instead of cumulative spike id (which is essentially a random number starting at 1)
temp_data_grouped['spike_id'] = temp_data_grouped.groupby(temp_data_grouped['extreme_date_time'].dt.date).cumcount() + 1


#retrieve only relevant columns from temp_data_grouped:
excursions = pd.DataFrame({'spike_numb':temp_data_grouped['spike_id'].values,
                           'spike_extreme_temp': temp_data_grouped['extreme_temp'].values,
                            'spike_extreme_date_time':temp_data_grouped['extreme_date_time'].values,
                             'spike_duration_mins': temp_data_grouped['spike_duration_mins'].values,
                              "spike_date": temp_data_grouped['spike_start_time'].dt.date})


excursions = excursions.to_dict('records')

print(df_last_spike_of_day.head(50))
